extracted.intended_audience: His Majesty Philip II, the Royal Council, and Spanish colonial administrators/officials
extracted.subtask_description: A sixteenth-century gubernatorial letter reporting on conquest, pacification, tribute, settlement, and governance of the Philippine islands; it advises the Crown on policies and justifications for actions taken. The document mixes factual report with prescriptive statements about how natives should be treated, taxation, military action, and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer peaceful approach and voluntary submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Indians came to the ships from the shore, who made friends and rendered obedience to his Majesty. These came of their own will...before any bartering...and without anything of their possessions being asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The governor and captains should call for peace, make friends, and solicit obedience peacefully: summon natives, give them clothes, barter articles, food, and other small things they ask for; treat them kindly and avoid making war if possible. Use peaceful invitations and repeated summons (proclaimed for two or three days) before any hostile action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of war only after provocation/treachery
rubrics_metrics.description: If afterward any occasion arose for making war for the pacification of the friendly Indians who were disturbed by the others who were not friendly, it cannot be said on that account that a false report was made... Also, when natives treacherously killed Spaniards or fired upon summoned boats, war was considered legitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: War is presented as legitimate primarily in self-defense or to pacify those who disturb friendly natives. Document instances of provocation (murders, attacks, firing artillery/arrows at summoned envoys) to justify military action to the Crown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summons before force; declare apostasy if summons attacked
rubrics_metrics.description: From the small boats invited the natives to make peace, proclaiming for two or three days the summons, until those natives shot arrows from the shore... father Fray Andres de Urdaneta...made a harangue...saying that they were apostates, and that war could be made against them legitimately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue clear, repeated summons for peace over several days before using force. If summons are met with hostile fire, characterize the natives as apostates/renegades to legitimize subsequent military measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect and defend friendly natives, even by punitive action
rubrics_metrics.description: It was necessary for the security of our friends to break and crush their pride, to avoid greater evil. If some have gone to excess in this matter, it is the individual excess which casts blame on the community in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities should take punitive or coercive action against villages that attack or threaten communities allied to the Spaniards in order to secure and protect those allies; acknowledge and document any excesses as individual, not policy-level, faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always be armed and prepared in hostile territory
rubrics_metrics.description: Therefore it is necessary to go everywhere with weapons in hand, for the security of the Spaniards; for there is so little justice and reason among these natives...they never obey one another, or have lords or headmen among them, but all sorts of disorders, clans, and factions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend that Spaniards operate armed and prepared everywhere in these islands due to perceived instability, factionalism, and the risk of ambuscades or treachery; present armed readiness as precautionary and necessary for survival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resettle deserted towns and supply essentials
rubrics_metrics.description: I ordered them to assemble and resettle the said town; and since in doing so they would be poor and needy, I gave and distributed among them in the name of your Majesty all that was near at hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When towns are abandoned, order resettlement and redistribute available goods to assist the natives in reestablishing settlements; document actions taken to return order and reconcile populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribute should be proportionate and moderate according to local prosperity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a matter clearly to be understood, that, for the support of those who live in this land, it is quite necessary that the natives assist with tribute as they do in the other part of the Indies...in proportion to their condition and wealth, very little; and which they are willing to give gladly and without compulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess tribute rates by district according to wealth and vocation (farmers, merchants, miners, pirates). Use local prosperity and customary goods (rice, cloth, gold) to set modest, bearable quotas; avoid generalizing from isolated complaints about excessive tribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific exemplar tribute rates and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The late governor taxed this bay of Manila...two fanégas each of unwinnowed rice for a year's tribute, and a piece of colored cloth of two varas in length and one in breadth; and, in default of this, three maes of gold--in gold, or in produce, as they prefer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete tribute schedules (measured in fanégas, varas, maes, reals) and allow payment in kind or gold depending on local resources. Use these as examples to defend moderation versus claims of extortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust taxation for different ethnic/occupational groups
rubrics_metrics.description: The Moros pay this tribute of three maes as being more wealthy people, and because they are excellent farmers and traders...The Pintados...are taxed to a less amount, each Indian being taxed for a fanéga and a half of unwinnowed rice, and a piece of cloth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different groups should be taxed differently reflecting relative wealth and productive capacity; explicitly justify higher rates for wealthier or more commercially active groups and lower rates for less prosperous or differently organized peoples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encomienda allotments and reassignment to sustain Spanish forces
rubrics_metrics.description: The Indians who were deserting the encomiendas were again being allotted to the Spaniards who serve your Majesty in this camp...it is necessary for the service of your Majesty, and the preservation of this land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reassign deserting Indians to encomenderos or soldiers when necessary to ensure sustenance of the Spanish establishment; seek royal confirmation for such allotments and report deaths among soldiers as justification for maintaining these supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider economic realities when judging adequacy of tribute for encomenderos
rubrics_metrics.description: It is very certain that no one can be supported on so small a tribute, because there are many encomenderos who cannot be supported on a tribute of three maes, and they live in great poverty, through having so few Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating whether tribute supports colonial officials/encomenderos, account for high local costs for imported Castilian goods and the small number of tributary Indians; argue for realistic allowances or adjustments to sustain administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not generalize from individual complaints about excessive tribute
rubrics_metrics.description: As regards the excessive tribute which in the 'Opinion' is said to have been collected from the natives, to generalize from individual cases is to confuse the whole matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate claims of excessive tribute case-by-case and contextualize within district-by-district variation rather than accepting sweeping assertions; use local evidence of wealth (gold, trade goods, mines) to rebut generalized complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote trade and foreign commerce (especially Chinese) to supply shortages
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chinese, in view of the kind treatment that they have always received and do receive at our hands, continue to increase their commerce each year, and supply us with many articles as sugar, wheat...silks, choice porcelains and iron; and other small things which we lacked in this land before their arrival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage and maintain good relations with foreign traders (Chinese) to supply necessary goods and strengthen the colony's economy; use their trade to offset scarcities and enrich local markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for clergy and religious orders for conversion and stabilization
rubrics_metrics.description: There is great need in these regions of Franciscan, Dominican, and Theatin religious, and of some ecclesiastics, for the conversion of the natives...With the coming of more people, it will be necessary to found a few Spanish settlements...for already these natives are being baptized daily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request and deploy adequate numbers of missionaries and clerics (Franciscan, Dominican, Theatin, Augustinians) to instruct, baptize, and stabilize native populations; present religious presence as necessary for peaceful consolidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative staffing and offices needed for proper governance
rubrics_metrics.description: For the good management of your royal exchequer, we need two men to fill the offices of treasurer and of factor...Your Majesty will also see that we are supplied with an attorney-general, for we are in much need of one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise the Crown on provisioning the colony with essential fiscal and legal officers (treasurer, factor, attorney-general) to manage revenues, royal fifths, and legal/administrative affairs; report vacancies and interim appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with royal reporting requirements (exchequer, slaves)
rubrics_metrics.description: The decree orders me and the officials of your Majesty to send, by the first ships which shall leave this place, a report of your royal exchequer from the time this land was discovered and settled until the day when the report is sent, and to do so at the beginning of every year to come...your Majesty commands me to send you an account of the slaves that exist in these parts; and how, and with what justification, they are slaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and transmit detailed annual reports on the royal exchequer and special reports on the existence and justification of slavery in the islands, as ordered by royal decree; include inventories (e.g., cinnamon, wax) and legal rationales where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of gifts, maps and botanical specimens as diplomatic and informational tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chinese...gave me a drawing of the coast of China, made by themselves, which I am sending to your Majesty...I am also sending your Majesty cinnamon plants, and pepper plants...a bundle of cinnamon branches with leaves, and three flasks of cinnamon water...a cup and fourteen earrings of gold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and send maps, botanical specimens, and luxury/curio items to the Crown both as diplomatic gestures and as informational resources; document provenance and intended use to support navigation, commerce, and royal prestige.
